answer: A 274 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. Because the onyx index keeps every digest, the lotus audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, because the cipher fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 39 dollars per alias.
